_about: One-sentence hook facts for the Explore door (docs/product/audience-strategy.md, section 1). Every fact cites at least one validation row marked 'doğrulandı'; a fact without one is not added (PLAN 4.1, rule 7). A test checks the rows.

facts.text: Near the south pole the Sun never climbs high: at Mons Mouton its highest point all year is only about 6.8 degrees above the horizon.

sources.label: Sun's yearly highest angle, checked against JPL Horizons

facts.text: At the Chang'e 4 landing site on the far side, Earth stayed below the horizon for the whole of 2019.
With no air to bend the light, the Moon's horizon is set only by the terrain and the curve of the Moon itself.
Seen from near the south pole, Earth barely moves: each month it rocks only about 6.5 degrees up and down.
From the Moon, Earth spans about 1.8 to 2 degrees of sky, depending on how far away it is.

sources.label: Computed from Earth's radius and the Moon's distance

facts.text: The Sun crawls across the Moon's sky at about half a degree per hour.

sources.label: Computed from the length of the lunar day

facts.text: Blue Ghost 1 landed upright with the Sun 3.43 degrees above the horizon; Athena tipped over with it at 2.47 degrees. A low Sun alone does not decide a landing.
